55:- `run_command.sh` uses paths relative to its working directory, never absolute paths into the run directory, and writes only under `out/` or temporary files. The concurrency probe and evaluation run it from sibling work directories that link the same trees (see Concurrency probe). Harness and repair prompts state this requirement.
56:- Optional unit files (U50): `run_units.sh` and `units.json`, used only by the unit equivalence check (U51) and the unit-mode concurrency probe. `units.json` is exactly `{"units": [...]}` with at least four entries, in the order the published full run processes them, each exactly `{id, outputs, cost_s}`: `id` is a unique string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:+=-]{0,127}$` that identifies that unit to `run_units.sh`; `outputs` is a non-empty array of unique relative paths naming that unit's result files under `out/`, each one or more `/`-separated components made of `[A-Za-z0-9._+=-]`, none of them `.` or `..`; `cost_s` is a finite positive number, the unit's own seconds as recorded in the reproduce run's logs or outputs. `bash harness/run_units.sh <id>...` runs the exact measured command of `run_command.sh` (same binary, configuration, environment and scale) restricted to the listed units (one or more), in the order given, by one of two means: the published program's own subset selection when it takes effect, or otherwise a restricted copy of the prepared input list that the measured command reads, holding only the listed units' original records copied byte for byte in the list's own format, written under `out/` or a temporary directory and passed through an argument, configuration value or environment variable the measured command already accepts. Either way it retains the measured baseline's per-unit code, parameters and inputs exactly as `run_command.sh` runs them, including any documented setup or anchors repairs the measured baseline already carries: the reference is the measured baseline, not the pristine upstream program, and no new code change is allowed. A path-rule conflict that `run_command.sh` already has is inherited and recorded separately; the unit files add none. Reader evidence (run10_diff, 2026-11-01): the entry point's command-line selector exists but has no effect; the measured command reads a prepared input list whose path it already accepts, a restricted list of original records under `out/` adds no write elsewhere, and the per-unit code differences earlier subsetting attempts were flagged for are inherited repairs. Owner decision 2026-11-01: allow selection of original prepared input records while retaining the measured baseline's per-unit code, parameters and inputs. It obeys every `run_command.sh` rule (relative paths, writes only under `out/` or temporary files, no `CUDA_MPS_*` changes), writes each listed unit's `outputs` under `out/` at the same paths as the full run, and propagates the exit status. Under `args.harness_from`, each of the two files present in the source is copied with its exact bytes and recorded in `C/harness_source.json` like the scripts. Files present in `A/harness/` are uploaded with the initial harness upload (same encoding and batching), never later. No repair changes them: after every setup or anchors repair the pipeline restores their bytes (or their absence), as it restores `run_evaluation.sh`. The harness agent is not asked to write them; fresh harness generation is unchanged. The unit equivalence check (U51) and the probe's comparison with the frozen baseline outputs (see Concurrency probe) are their validation.
74:  1. Sample: the four units chosen by the unit-mode sample rule (see Concurrency probe), in sample order.
81:## Standalone unit probe (U52)
84:- In unit-probe mode reproduce runs the box probe, harness copy or generation, upload and setup with its repairs exactly as usual, and requires the unit files exactly as units-check mode does (`parse` before the harness upload). Before the harness upload it also takes the sample by the unit-mode sample rule and computes the SHA-256 of every output path of the four sample units under `reference`; a missing or unreadable reference file fails reproduce with `error_class: parse`. It writes those digests to `A/results/reproduce/units_reference.json` in the reference-file shape (see Concurrency probe, "Output checks").
102:  - `concurrency`: the validated `concurrency.json` object (see Concurrency probe), or null when the probe did not run or its output is missing or invalid.
106:## Concurrency probe: calibration of same-GPU headroom
120:- Unit mode (U50b). The probe script's second form, `python3 -I profiler/concurrency_probe.py --units <run_units_file> <units_json> <out_dir> <budget_s> <reference_json>`, runs unit mode. Only the standalone unit probe (U52) invokes it; the profile stage always runs command mode exactly as described above (owner decision 2026-11-02: the standalone route; unit mode inside the profile stage is deferred). Unit mode never uses MPS and does not look for the MPS binary. It compares the same four units run in one invocation, as separate invocations one after another, and as separate invocations at once, holding inputs and per-unit configuration fixed and checking every output byte for byte. Owner decision 2026-11-01: the smallest bounded experiment that resolves whether a CPU-only baseline's units gain throughput when run at once, with only the pipeline changes that comparison needs. Reader evidence (blind-01 run9): units are distinct inputs, selectable by restricting the prepared input list to original records (the command-line selector has no effect); each unit writes its own result files at the same paths in full and subset runs, with no run-specific content, and its outputs repeat bit for bit; the reproduce logs record every unit's cost; whether a unit reads state left by earlier units of the same invocation is unknown, which the comparison with the recorded baseline tests; four median-cost units selected on their own reproduced run9's recorded result files byte for byte (run10, U51); units take 1 to 10 min with a cost spread over 50%; the baseline's own threads already use at least half the logical CPUs. Command mode would instead run three whole commands of 1 to 2 h and compare no outputs.
144:- The standalone unit probe (U52) validates a unit-mode file against the exact shape above, including each batch factor and `factor` as the largest batch factor. A measured unit-mode factor below 1.05 is a valid negative finding.
170:- `factor` is the packet's `concurrency.factor`: the same-GPU concurrent throughput measured during calibration (see Concurrency probe). When the packet has no `concurrency` key, `concurrency` is null, or its factor is null or below 1, whole-workload methods use `k=1` (bound 1, infeasible): missing measurements never manufacture headroom. A `concurrency` value that is neither null nor an object, or a factor that is neither null nor a finite number, fails parsing.

     2	# run_units.sh - the measured baseline restricted to original prepared input records.
     3	#
     4	# Invoked as:  bash harness/run_units.sh <system_id:kind>...   (working directory = the shared run directory, or a sibling
     5	# work directory that links baseline-published/, data/ and harness/). Command paths are relative;
     6	# absolute PATH entries and TMPDIR are inherited from run_command.sh (see REPORT.md).
     7	# PATH entries are resolved from this working directory because the published
     8	# FroDock adapter changes directory into a temporary stage directory.
     9	#
    10	# Representative scale (EXECUTION.json, fixed): the 8 preregistered PINDER-S apo-paired systems in
    11	# data/selection.json; requested holo/apo jobs only, n_solutions=50, mpi_np=8, force=false,
    12	# docked by the published `pinder_methods predict --method frodock` and scored by the published
    13	# `pinder_eval` (50 decoys per selected job). FroDock is CPU + MPI only: no GPU is used (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="",
    14	# GPU count 0). CUDA MPS variables are inherited unchanged.
    15	#
    16	# Output (stdout+stderr of both published commands): out/run_command/run_command.log
    17	#   decoys:  out/results/frodock/<pinder_id>/{holo,apo}_decoys/model_<rank>.pdb
    18	#   scores:  out/results/frodock_metrics.csv, out/results/frodock_leaderboard.csv
    19	# Exit status: nonzero if either published command fails.
    20	set -Eeuo pipefail
    21	[ "$#" -gt 0 ] || { echo "ERROR: at least one system_id:kind is required" >&2; exit 2; }
    22	
    23	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ complete environment
    24	export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""          # CPU/MPI-only baseline
    25	BASELINE_GPU_COUNT=0
    26	N_SOLUTIONS=50
    27	MPI_NP=8
    28	FORCE=false
    29	EVAL_MAX_WORKERS=8
    30	METHOD=frodock
    31	export PINDER_BASE_DIR=data
    32	export PINDER_RELEASE=2024-02
    33	export LOG_LEVEL=INFO
    34	export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
    35	unset PINDER_DATA_DIR || true
    36	# CUDA toolchain selection (same ls-checked rule as setup.sh; not used by the CPU baseline)
    37	CUDA_SEL=""
    38	for root in /usr/local/cuda /usr/lib/cuda; do
    39	  if ls "$root/bin/nvcc" "$root/include/cuda_runtime.h" "$root/lib64/libcudart.so" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    40	    CUDA_SEL="toolkit_root:$root"; export PATH="$root/bin:$PATH"; export CUDAToolkit_ROOT="$root"; break
    41	  fi
    42	done
    43	if [ -z "$CUDA_SEL" ] && ls /usr/bin/nvcc /usr/include/cuda_runtime.h /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudart.so >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    44	  CUDA_SEL="distro:/usr/bin/nvcc"
    45	fi
    46	[ -n "$CUDA_SEL" ] || { echo "ERROR: no complete CUDA layout found (same rule as setup.sh)" >&2; exit 1; }
    47	VENV=baseline-published/venv
    48	VPY="$VENV/bin/python"
    49	export PATH="$PWD/baseline-published/frodock/bin:$PWD/$VENV/bin:$PATH"
    50	export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
    51	
    52	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ output locations (logs preserved)
    53	RUN_DIR="out/run_command"
    54	RESULTS="out/results"
    55	mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR/history"
    56	TS="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%NZ)"
    57	if [ -e "$RUN_DIR/run_command.log" ]; then
    58	  mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR/history/$TS"
    59	  mv "$RUN_DIR"/*.log "$RUN_DIR"/*.yaml "$RUN_DIR"/*.json "$RUN_DIR"/*.tar.gz "$RUN_DIR/history/$TS/" 2>/dev/null || true
    60	fi
    61	# Preserve decoys and scoring output from earlier invocations as well as logs.
    62	if [ -d "$RESULTS" ]; then
    63	  mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR/history/$TS"
    64	  mv "$RESULTS" "$RUN_DIR/history/$TS/results"

    68	export TMPDIR="$PWD/out/tmp"

    70	for f in "$VPY" "$VENV/bin/pinder_methods" "$VENV/bin/pinder_eval" data/selection.json data/frodock/frodock_setup.csv; do

    72	done

    87	"$VPY" - "$RUN_DIR/frodock_config.yaml" "$RESULTS/frodock_setup.csv" data/selection.json \
    88	    "$METHOD" "$N_SOLUTIONS" "$MPI_NP" "$FORCE" "$EVAL_MAX_WORKERS" "$BASELINE_GPU_COUNT" <<'PY'
    89	import json, os, sys, yaml
    90	import pandas as pd
    91	from pinder.core import get_index
    92	cfg = yaml.safe_load(open(sys.argv[1])); jobs = pd.read_csv(sys.argv[2]); sel = json.load(open(sys.argv[3]))
    93	idx = get_index()
    94	s = idx[idx["pinder_s"].astype(bool)]
    95	apo = s[s["apo_R"].astype(bool) & s["apo_L"].astype(bool)]
    96	ids = sorted(set(apo["id"]))[: sel["n"]]
    97	print(f"PINDER_S_SYSTEM_COUNT={s['id'].nunique()}")
    98	print(f"PINDER_S_APO_PAIRED_COUNT={apo['id'].nunique()}")
    99	print("SELECTED_IDS=" + json.dumps(ids))
   100	errs = []
   101	if sys.argv[4:] != ["frodock", "50", "8", "false", "8", "0"]: errs.append("actual command parameters differ from fixed configuration")
   102	if os.environ.get("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES") != "": errs.append("CPU baseline must expose zero GPUs")
   103	if os.environ.get("PINDER_BASE_DIR") != "data" or os.environ.get("PINDER_RELEASE") != "2024-02": errs.append("dataset environment differs from fixed configuration")
   104	if ids != sel["ids"]: errs.append("selection from index differs from data/selection.json")
   105	if sel["n"] != 8 or len(ids) != 8: errs.append("representative scale must contain exactly 8 systems")
   106	if cfg != {"n_solutions": 50, "mpi_np": 8, "force": False}: errs.append(f"config {cfg} is not the published representative config")
   107	if sorted(set(jobs["id"])) != sorted(ids): errs.append("frodock_setup.csv ids differ from selection")
   108	if sorted(set(jobs["kind"])) != ["apo", "holo"] or len(jobs) != 2 * len(ids): errs.append("frodock_setup.csv is not holo+apo for every id")
   109	if set(zip(jobs["id"], jobs["kind"])) != {(pid, kind) for pid in ids for kind in ("holo", "apo")}: errs.append("frodock_setup.csv lacks an expected id/pairing")
   110	print(f"CONFIG method=frodock subset=pinder-s pairs=holo,apo n_jobs={len(jobs)} n_solutions={cfg.get('n_solutions')} "
   111	      f"mpi_np={cfg.get('mpi_np')} force={cfg.get('force')} CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='{os.environ.get('CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES')}' "
   112	      f"host_nproc={os.cpu_count()} PINDER_BASE_DIR={os.environ.get('PINDER_BASE_DIR')}")
   113	if errs:
   114	    sys.exit("ERROR: " + "; ".join(errs))

   116	echo "GPU_COUNT=$BASELINE_GPU_COUNT CUDA_SELECTION=$CUDA_SEL MPIRUN=$(command -v mpirun) FRODOCK_BIN=$(dirname "$(command -v frodock_mpi_gcc)")"

   132	raw = target.read_bytes().splitlines(keepends=True)
   133	reader = csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(b"".join(raw).decode("utf-8"), newline=""), strict=True)
   134	rows = list(reader)
   135	if reader.fieldnames != ["id", "kind", "receptor", "ligand"] or not rows:
   136	    sys.exit("ERROR: unexpected prepared manifest schema")
   137	if len(raw) != len(rows) + 1 or any(not line.endswith(b"\n") for line in raw):
   138	    sys.exit("ERROR: expected the original newline-terminated one-line-per-record format")
   139	keys = [row["id"] + ":" + row["kind"] for row in rows]
   140	if len(set(keys)) != len(keys):
   141	    sys.exit("ERROR: duplicate prepared unit")
   142	if any(not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:+=-]{0,127}", key)
   143	       or key not in keys for key in requested):
   144	    sys.exit("ERROR: unknown or invalid requested unit")
   145	target.write_bytes(raw[0] + b"".join(raw[keys.index(key) + 1] for key in requested))
   146	print("RESTRICTED_UNITS=" + ",".join(requested))

**B. Prediction 6**

`C:21–23`: `subset_wall_s=1080.9474446559998`, `cost_sum_s=1008.9430003166199`, `cost_ratio=1.0713662162449058`. Independently recomputed same ratio. **C. What writes where**

The question's background overstates what earlier reports established. If index is missing, separate processes can all observe absence, fetch it, and write same fixed `index.parquet` without shown lock/atomic replacement around dataframe serialization (`core_index_utils.py.txt:125–134`).    106	## Concurrency probe: calibration of same-GPU headroom
   107	- Purpose: measure, before any prediction or method exists, how much more throughput one GPU gives when the unchanged published command runs several times at once. This measured factor is the only source of same-GPU headroom for bounds. No model call is involved.
   108	- When the profile command exits 0 and the profile gate passes, the pipeline uploads trusted `m5/concurrency_probe.py` to remote `profiler/` and, through boxrun as operation `concurrency` with the resolved `profile` budget, runs `python3 -I profiler/concurrency_probe.py harness/run_command.sh out/concurrency <budget_s>` from the shared run directory. Remote `out/concurrency/` is cleared first. Fetched files land in `A/results/profile/out/concurrency/`; the log is `A/results/profile/<receipt-id>.log`. There is no agent repair and no execution retry. Probe receipts count toward profile v1 `usd` and `gpu_s` like other box receipts.
   109	- Each invocation runs `bash harness/run_command.sh` with its working directory set to a fresh `concurrency-work/<label>/` under the shared run directory. That directory holds a symlink to every top-level entry of the shared run directory except `out`, `profiler`, `concurrency-work` and `evaluation-work`, plus an empty `out/` directory. Labels are `single-1`, `single-2`, `single-3`, `n2-1`, `n2-2`, `n4-1` to `n4-4`. Each invocation's stdout and stderr go to `out/concurrency/logs/<label>.log` of the shared run directory. The environment is inherited unchanged apart from the MPS variables below. Nsight is not used.
   110	- MPS: when `nvidia-cuda-mps-control` is on PATH, the probe starts a user-level daemon (`nvidia-cuda-mps-control -d`) with `CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY` and `CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY` set to fresh directories under `concurrency-work/`, passes both variables to every invocation, and stops the daemon (`echo quit | nvidia-cuda-mps-control` with the same variables) before exiting, including after failures and on SIGTERM. If the daemon fails to start or any invocation fails under MPS, the probe stops the daemon, records `mps_failed: true`, and repeats the complete probe once without MPS in fresh work directories. Without the binary there is no MPS and `mps_failed` is false.
   111	- MPS use is verified, not assumed. The daemon's `control.log` in its `CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY` records each client connection as a line containing `NEW CLIENT <pid> from user <uid>`. After each single run and each batch under MPS, the probe counts these lines (case-sensitive substring `NEW CLIENT `, followed by an integer pid and ` from user `). The count must have grown by at least the number of copies just run (1 for a single run, n for a batch of n). A missing or unreadable log, or a smaller increase, means the copies did not run under MPS: the probe treats this like an invocation failure under MPS (stop the daemon, `mps_failed: true`, repeat the complete probe once without MPS). `mps: true` is therefore recorded only when every counted measurement was verified to run under MPS. No log content enters `concurrency.json`.
   112	- Sequence: three single runs one after another, then 2 copies started together, then 4 copies started together. Wall seconds come from a monotonic clock around each subprocess; a batch's wall runs from launching its first copy to the exit of its last. `T1` is the median of the single walls. A single run that exits nonzero stops the probe with a null factor. Before each batch, the batch is skipped when `n * T1` exceeds `0.9 * budget_s` minus the probe's elapsed seconds. A batch counts only when every copy exits 0. For a counted batch, `factor_n = n * T1 / wall_n`.
   113	- `out/concurrency/concurrency.json` is written atomically with exactly `{mps, mps_failed, single_wall_s, batches, factor}`:
   114	  - `mps`: boolean, true when the recorded measurements ran under MPS; `mps_failed`: boolean;
   115	  - `single_wall_s`: array of exactly three entries, each a finite positive number or null (failed or not run);
   116	  - `batches`: exactly two rows, in order n=2 then n=4, each exactly `{n, wall_s, all_ok, skipped, factor}`; `wall_s` and `factor` are finite positive numbers or null, `all_ok` and `skipped` are booleans, and `factor` is null unless the batch counted;
   117	  - `factor`: the largest counted `factor_n`, or null when any single run failed or no batch counted.
   118	  The probe exits 0 whenever it writes the file, including with a null factor, and 2 when it cannot. It does not check output correctness: it measures throughput only.
   119	- The probe never fails the profile stage and never changes the profile gate. A probe timeout, nonzero exit, or missing or invalid file gives packet `concurrency: null` and `headroom: null`. The pipeline validates the file against the exact shape above before copying it into the packet.
   120	- Unit mode (U50b). The probe script's second form, `python3 -I profiler/concurrency_probe.py --units <run_units_file> <units_json> <out_dir> <budget_s> <reference_json>`, runs unit mode. Only the standalone unit probe (U52) invokes it; the profile stage always runs command mode exactly as described above (owner decision 2026-11-02: the standalone route; unit mode inside the profile stage is deferred). Unit mode never uses MPS and does not look for the MPS binary. It compares the same four units run in one invocation, as separate invocations one after another, and as separate invocations at once, holding inputs and per-unit configuration fixed and checking every output byte for byte. Owner decision 2026-11-01: the smallest bounded experiment that resolves whether a CPU-only baseline's units gain throughput when run at once, with only the pipeline changes that comparison needs. Reader evidence (blind-01 run9): units are distinct inputs, selectable by restricting the prepared input list to original records (the command-line selector has no effect); each unit writes its own result files at the same paths in full and subset runs, with no run-specific content, and its outputs repeat bit for bit; the reproduce logs record every unit's cost; whether a unit reads state left by earlier units of the same invocation is unknown, which the comparison with the recorded baseline tests; four median-cost units selected on their own reproduced run9's recorded result files byte for byte (run10, U51); units take 1 to 10 min with a cost spread over 50%; the baseline's own threads already use at least half the logical CPUs. Command mode would instead run three whole commands of 1 to 2 h and compare no outputs.
   121	- Sample: units sorted by `cost_s` ascending, ties by manifest order; the sample is the four consecutive sorted units starting at sorted position floor((N - 4) / 2), N being the number of units, kept in that order as sample positions 0 to 3. Units near the median cost keep concurrent invocations of similar length, so a batch runs at its full width for nearly its whole wall time; the factor therefore describes typical units, not the shortest or longest.

   129	- Output checks. The reference file `<reference_json>` is exactly `{"sha256": {<output path>: <64 lowercase hex digits>}}`, keyed by every output path of the four sample units and nothing else. After `a-1`, every output path of every sample unit under `a-1`'s `out/` must exist and have the SHA-256 recorded for that path (`baseline_match`); a file missing under `a-1`, a path missing from the reference, or a reference file that is unreadable or not of that shape is a mismatch.    130	- Budget: before each arm, that arm and every later arm are skipped when its estimate exceeds `0.9 * budget_s` minus the probe's elapsed seconds. The estimate is the sum of the sample's `cost_s` for `a-1`, and `a-1`'s measured wall for every later arm.
   131	- Resource use. For each invocation, from `os.wait4` on its process (which includes its waited-for descendants): `cpu_s` (user plus system seconds), `max_rss_kb`, `nivcsw` (involuntary context switches), `inblock` and `oublock`.    132	- Shared writes. Each arm records `shared_changes`: the number of non-directory entries under the shared run directory, outside `out/`, `concurrency-work/` and `profiler/`, that appeared, disappeared, or changed size or modification time (nanoseconds) between a snapshot taken just before the arm's first launch and one taken just after its last exit.    133	- In unit mode `out/concurrency/concurrency.json` is written atomically with exactly `{mode, mps, mps_failed, outcome, units_total, sample, baseline_match, outputs_match, serial_wall_s, separate_wall_s, batches, arms, nproc, mem_total_kb, factor}`:
